claim: Each role used by an identity pool needs a trust policy so that only Amazon Cognito can assume it for authenticated users of that identity pool: the principal is cognito-identity.amazonaws.com, the aud condition must match the identity pool ID, and the amr claim must contain authenticated.
question: What must the trust policy of an IAM role used by a Cognito identity pool contain?

values.display: can only be assumed by Amazon Cognito

qualifiers.scope: IAM roles assumed through a Cognito identity pool

evidence.quote: It is important to add the appropriate trust policy for each role so that it can only be assumed by Amazon Cognito for authenticated users in your identity pool.

This policy allows federated users from `cognito-identity.amazonaws.com` (the issuer of the OpenID Connect token) to assume this role. Additionally, the policy restricts the `aud` of the token, in this case the identity pool ID, to match the identity pool. Finally, the policy specifies that one of the array members of the multi-value `amr` claim of the token issued by the Amazon Cognito `GetOpenIdToken` API action has the value `authenticated`.

note: d099. The 2025-08-01 history row is for the numbers+changes lens.

claim: Rule-based role mapping evaluates rules in order and uses the IAM role of the first matching rule; if no rule matches, the Role resolution setting either uses the default authenticated role or denies the request.
question: Which IAM role does a Cognito identity pool use when several rules exist or none match?

values.display: the IAM role for the first matching rule is used

qualifiers.scope: Cognito identity pool rule-based role mapping

evidence.quote: Rules are evaluated in order, and the IAM role for the first matching rule is used, unless `CustomRoleArn` is specified to override the order.
If no rules match, the **Role resolution** setting is applied to either **Use default authenticated role** or **Deny request**.

claim: A user pool group can carry an IAM role; when a user is in several groups, the cognito:preferred_role claim of the ID token is set to the role of the group with the best (lowest) precedence value, and the identity pool can use it to issue credentials.
question: How does a Cognito identity pool pick a role for a user who belongs to several user pool groups?

values.display: assign an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role to a group
The group with the better (lower) precedence will be chosen

qualifiers.scope: Cognito user pool groups with identity pools

evidence.quote: You can assign an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role to a group to define the permissions for members of a group.
The group with the better (lower) precedence will be chosen and its associated IAM role will be applied.
+ The `cognito:preferred_role` claim is set to the role from the group with the best (lowest) `Precedence` value.

claim: Amazon Cognito creates a user group for each OIDC, SAML and social identity provider added to a user pool, and each automatically generated IdP user profile is added to that group; groups have no additional cost.
question: Does Cognito group federated users from one identity provider automatically?

values.display: creates a user group for each OIDC, SAMl, and social
no additional cost for using groups

evidence.quote: Each unique automatically-generated IdP user profile is automatically added to this group.
There is no additional cost for using groups within a user pool.

note: d110. First display wording follows the page's own spelling 'SAMl'.

claim: To protect a REST API with a Cognito user pool, you create a COGNITO_USER_POOLS authorizer in API Gateway and enable it on API methods; the client signs in, gets an identity or access token, and sends it, typically in the Authorization header, and the call succeeds only with a valid token.
question: How does an API Gateway REST API use a Cognito user pool to authorize calls, and where does the client send the token?

evidence.quote: To use an Amazon Cognito user pool with your API, you must first create an authorizer of the `COGNITO_USER_POOLS` type and then configure an API method to use that authorizer.

The API call succeeds only if the required token is supplied and the supplied token is valid, otherwise, the client isn't authorized to make the call because the client did not have credentials that could be authorized.
Use a client-specific framework to call the deployed API Gateway API and supply the appropriate token in the `Authorization` header.

note: d095. The display 'the request's `Authorization` header' comes from the page's long sentence; the quote list holds the Authorization-header line.

claim: With a Cognito user pool authorizer, the identity token authorizes API calls based on the signed-in user's identity claims, and the access token authorizes calls based on custom scopes of access-protected resources.
question: When should an API Gateway Cognito authorizer accept the ID token versus the access token?

values.display: based on identity claims of the signed-in user

qualifiers.scope: API Gateway REST APIs with a Cognito user pool authorizer

evidence.quote: The identity token is used to authorize API calls based on identity claims of the signed-in user. The access token is used to authorize API calls based on the custom scopes of specified access-protected resources.

claim: To let a user sign in with Cognito and also use temporary credentials with the permissions of an IAM role, use Cognito identity pools (federated identities) and set the API Gateway method authorization type to AWS_IAM.
question: Can API Gateway authorize callers with IAM using Cognito identity pool credentials?

evidence.quote: To let a user sign in using Amazon Cognito credentials and also obtain temporary credentials to use with the permissions of an IAM role, use [Amazon Cognito Federated Identities](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-identity.html). For each API resource endpoint HTTP method, set the authorization type, category `Method Execution`, to `AWS_IAM`.

claim: A user pool custom domain for managed login needs an SSL certificate managed with AWS Certificate Manager in US East (N. Virginia); Amazon Cognito creates a CloudFront distribution secured with that certificate, and you create a DNS record pointing to it.
question: Which Region must the ACM certificate for a Cognito custom domain be in, and what does Cognito create?

evidence.quote: Custom domains also require an SSL certificate for the custom domain, managed with AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in US East (N. Virginia). Amazon Cognito creates a Amazon CloudFront distribution, secured in transit with your ACM certificate.

claim: With a custom domain, users sign in to the application through managed login at your own web address instead of the default amazoncognito.com prefix domain.
question: Can Cognito managed login run on your own domain name?

evidence.quote: With a custom domain, users can sign in to your application using your own web address instead the default `amazoncognito.com` [prefix domain](cognito-user-pools-assign-domain-prefix.md).

claim: An identity pool provides temporary AWS credentials both to guest (unauthenticated) users and to authenticated users who received a token, and it is a store of user identifiers linked to external identity providers.
question: Who can receive temporary AWS credentials from a Cognito identity pool?

evidence.quote: Amazon Cognito identity pools provide temporary AWS credentials for users who are guests (unauthenticated) and for users who have been authenticated and received a token. An identity pool is a store of user identifiers linked to your external identity providers.
